title: Biography of Richard Cowan: The Return of MarijuanaNews.com

content_html_sanitized:
Richard Cowan was born in Fort Worth, Texas, in 1940. He graduated from high school in Fort Worth in 1958. After graduating from Yale University in 1962 with a degree in Economics, he served in executive positions in various family companies, involved in manufacturing and natural resources, some of which were publicly owned. He has extensive experience in both business and public affairs.


At Yale, he was active in campus politics. He became Chairman of the Party of the Right in the Yale Political Union, where found that he loved to debate. He was also a founding member of Young Americans for Freedom, the national Conservative student group launched in 1960 by the late William F. Buckley, Jr., the leading Conservative intellectual of the 20th century. Buckley's friendship became a lifelong influence on Cowan. 


Cowan has been involved in the marijuana reform movement, almost since its inception. On December 6, 1972 Buckley’s National Review magazine published (as a cover article) Cowan’s "Why Conservatives Should Support the Legalization of Marijuana." 


In his book Smoke and Mirrors, the late Dan Baum said that this article "opened a second front in the War on Drugs." Time Magazine and the New York Times even carried stories about the article, because it seemed so improbable.

Fourteen years later, on December 5, 1986, National Review also published (again as a cover article) Cowan’s "How the Narcs Created Crack." 

See https://marijuananews.com/articles/how-the-narcs-created-crack-by-richard-c-cowan/legacy

This article has been cited in various scholarly journals as the origin of the economics of contraband, "The Iron Law of Prohibition: the harder the enforcement, the harder the drugs." See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_law_of_prohibition


Cowan also served as the Executive Director of the National Organization for the Reform of Marijuana Laws, from 1992 to 1995, and he was also a founding member of the Drug Policy Foundation and at various times has been active in the Libertarian Party

When he was NORML Executive Director, the NORML Board included such figures as the late Dr. Lester Grinspoon, Nobel Laureate Kary Mullis, and Ann Druyan, co-producer of Cosmos (with her late husband, Carl Sagan), also Cato Institute’s David Boaz and others. As Executive Director of NORML, Cowan’s television appearances included interviews on numerous news programs, including CNN, and a variety of talk shows. 


In 1997 Cowan launched MarijuanaNews.com, which has been called one of the first “blogs” of any kind. 


Writings on other subjects have appeared in a variety of publications.

From 2000 to 2005 he did the 420 MarijuanaNews on Pot.TV,  one of the first Internet video “Podcasts”, before the word was invented.


He has debated in the Oxford Union,and has spoken before a committee of the Congress of the Republic of Mexico, and various American state legislatures, including his native Texas, arguing against cannabis prohibition.


Cowan has traveled extensively, and has lived in Fort Worth and Dallas, Texas, Vancouver, Canada, Amsterdam, and Haarlem, in the Netherlands, Washington, D. C., Irvine and Palm Springs, California, and Madrid, Spain. Currently, he lives in Valencia, Spain, where he is an economics consultant for a privately owned international investment company.


In May of 2024, Cowan became the CEO of WEED.DE, a German website devoted to helping Germans, and other EU citizens, get access to newly legalized medical and recreational cannabis as provided by the new German law. Cowan is especially focused on helping senior citizens exercise their rights. 


Cowan will be writing frequently for WEED.DE and these and other articles will be posted in English on MarijuanaNews.com.
